note: [agent-bulk] mcp2k numucc_em. 40 segments, 15 showers, 2 in scope (63034, 77063); the thirteen skipped are 1.6 cm and smaller and I did not look at them individually, though several are named below as non-members. drag_check both true, probe 206.2 px off centroid, not degenerate. r95 223.1 cm because of a 100 cm muon, so the default sweep was framed at +-223 cm; I judged the vertex from a --vtx-span 60 re-capture (shots-vtx/evt289246). VERTEX is good: at +-60 cm the star is a clean two-prong V and nothing else -- 16001 (100.7 cm, pdg 13, 169 points) one way and 16002 (15.9 cm, pdg 2212) the other, both correctly unowned. THE UNDER-CLUSTERING. Shower 63034 (264.0 MeV, 23 segments, conn 2) is a large, well-populated, clearly electromagnetic complex: its 23 members run 0 to 62.9 cm from its start at 0.0 to 21.3 deg, and its acceptance plot shows all 23 squares and NO non-member circle anywhere in the window out to 80 cm and 27 deg. What it is missing sits off the TOP of that plot: 77063 (2.5 cm) and 77064 (8.0 cm) -- one 38.2 MeV object, 10.5 cm of segment -- at 14.7 and 15.3 cm from 63034's start and 53.0 and 46.7 deg from its axis. I ran the correction-11 reconciliation before calling this: 63034's owner-grouped count is 23 and its cmp_div says 23, and 77063's owner-grouped count is 2 and its nseg is 2, so this is genuine non-membership and not the first-owner-wins artifact. THE ARGUMENT, and it is a transverse-radius argument rather than an angle one: at 15 cm and 50 deg the missing object is about 11.5 cm off the shower axis, and 63034 already accepts members at 20.9-21.3 deg at 25-30 cm, which is 9-11 cm off the same axis. So the shower's own accepted transverse reach is the same 11 cm; the piece is rejected only because it sits closer to the start, where the same transverse offset subtends a much larger angle. That is what a pure angular cone cut does near a shower start, and in liquid argon 11 cm is about 1.2 Moliere radii on a 264 MeV shower, i.e. exactly where the last ~10 percent of the energy lives. Adding it moves the shower from 264 to 302 MeV. THE WEAKNESS, and it is why this is likely rather than certain: 47-53 deg is a large angle to defend on a picture, and at az+085 the missing object reads as a compact blob beside the shower start rather than as an obvious part of the body. It is NOT a second photon: the display auto-slotted 63034 + 77063 and the vertex convention gives theta 1.1 deg -> 2.0 MeV and the axis convention theta 17.5 deg -> 30.6 MeV, i.e. the two objects lie in the same direction from the star (130 and 145 cm out) and cannot be a pi0 pair. That collinearity from the vertex is itself an argument that they are one object. A SEPARATE THING WORTH THE OWNER'S EYE, which I did not turn into the verdict: 63034 starts 130.2 cm from the neutrino vertex, 89.1 cm beyond the end of the 100.7 cm muon and at 43 deg to the muon direction. For a photon that is about five conversion lengths in liquid argon, a sub-percent proposition, so either this is a rare long conversion, or the 264 MeV shower does not belong to this neutrino interaction at all. The vertex itself is unambiguous (two prongs converge on it), so I did not record vertex-bad; but the association between that vertex and this shower is the weakest link in the event. PI0: no reco pi0 group, and none should be expected -- there is no second EM object in the event that is not part of 63034.
